name: Jeunesse Esch
content:
Jeunesse Esch, officially known as Association Sportive la Jeunesse d’Esch/Alzette, is a professional football club based in Esch-sur-Alzette in southwestern Luxembourg. Founded in 1907, the team competes in the top tier of Luxembourgish football, the National Division. The club plays its home matches at the Stade de la Frontière and is widely recognized as one of the most historic and successful football teams in the country.

Historically, Jeunesse Esch is the most successful club in Luxembourg, having won the national league title 28 times between 1921 and 2010, which remains a record. In addition to its league success, the club has also won the Luxembourg Cup multiple times and achieved several domestic doubles. Throughout its history, Jeunesse Esch has been a dominant force in Luxembourgish football and a regular participant in European competitions, although it has rarely progressed beyond the early rounds.

The club has undergone various changes over time, including a temporary name change during World War II under Nazi occupation, before returning to its original identity after the war. One of its most notable international moments came in 1973 when the team held Liverpool to a 1–1 draw at home in European competition. Despite fluctuations in performance in recent years, Jeunesse Esch remains an important and traditional club in Luxembourg’s football landscape.

name: F91 Dudelange
content:
F91 Dudelange is a professional football club based in the town of Dudelange in southern Luxembourg. Founded in 1991, the club was created through the merger of three local teams—Alliance Dudelange, Stade Dudelange, and US Dudelange—in an effort to strengthen football in the region both financially and competitively. It plays its home matches at the Stade Jos Nosbaum and competes in the Luxembourg National Division, the top tier of the country’s football system.

Domestically, F91 Dudelange has established itself as one of the most successful clubs in Luxembourg. Since its formation, the team has won the national league title 16 times and lifted the Luxembourg Cup on multiple occasions, becoming a dominant force especially from the late 1990s onward. The club quickly rose through the ranks after its creation and soon ended the long-standing dominance of other teams, building a reputation for consistent success in domestic competitions.

On the European stage, F91 Dudelange has achieved historic milestones for Luxembourgish football. The club became the first team from the country to reach the group stage of a major European competition when it qualified for the UEFA Europa League in the 2018–19 season, repeating the feat the following year. In the 2019–20 campaign, it also recorded Luxembourg’s first-ever group stage victory, highlighting its role in raising the international profile of football in Luxembourg.

name: CA Spora Luxembourg
content:
CA Spora Luxembourg was a historic football club based in Luxembourg City, founded in 1923 through the merger of Racing Club Luxembourg and Sporting Club Luxembourg. It quickly became one of the leading teams in the country, competing in the top division and playing a major role in the early development of Luxembourgish football. The club’s identity was closely tied to its blue and yellow colors and its strong presence in the capital.

During its early decades, Spora was one of the dominant forces in Luxembourg, frequently competing with Red Boys Differdange for national supremacy. Before World War II, the club enjoyed a golden era, winning multiple league titles and domestic cups. It continued to achieve success after the war, adding further championships and cup victories, and establishing itself as one of the most successful clubs in the country with a total of 11 league titles and 8 Luxembourg Cups.

On the international stage, Spora occasionally competed in European competitions, with one of its most notable moments coming in 1956 when it defeated Borussia Dortmund in a European Cup match. Although the club never progressed far in continental tournaments, it gained recognition for such achievements. In 2005, CA Spora Luxembourg ceased to exist after merging with other clubs to form Racing FC Union Luxembourg, marking the end of a significant chapter in Luxembourg’s football history.

name: Stade Dudelange
content:
Stade Dudelange was a football club based in Dudelange, in southern Luxembourg. Founded in 1913, it became one of the most prominent teams in the country and competed in the Luxembourg National Division, the top tier of domestic football. The club played its home matches at Stade Aloyse Meyer and built a strong reputation over several decades as a leading force in Luxembourgish football.

During its peak years, particularly in the 1940s, Stade Dudelange achieved remarkable success. The club won a total of 10 national league titles and 4 Luxembourg Cups, making it one of the most successful teams in the country’s history. Notably, it won a sequence of six consecutive league titles spanning the pre- and post-World War II period, a record that has never been matched.

During World War II, when Luxembourg was annexed by Nazi Germany, the club competed under the name FV Stadt Düdelingen in the Gauliga Moselland and even won the division in 1942. Despite its historical success, the club eventually declined and ceased to exist in 1991 after merging with Alliance Dudelange and US Dudelange to form F91 Dudelange, marking the end of its independent history.

name: CS Fola Esch
content:
CS Fola Esch, officially known as Cercle Sportif Fola Esch, is a football club based in Esch-sur-Alzette in southwestern Luxembourg. Founded in 1906, it is recognized as the oldest football club in the country. The team plays its home matches at the Stade Émile Mayrisch and has long been an important part of Luxembourgish football history.

The club enjoyed its greatest success in the early decades of the 20th century, winning multiple national championships and domestic cups between 1918 and 1930. After a long period without major trophies, Fola Esch experienced a revival in the 2010s, winning league titles in 2012–13, 2014–15, and 2020–21. Overall, the club has secured eight national championships and several Luxembourg Cup victories, reestablishing itself as one of the country’s notable teams.

Fola Esch has also participated in European competitions, including the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League qualifiers, though it has not progressed far in these tournaments. In recent years, the club has faced mixed performances domestically, including relegation from the top division in the 2024–25 season. Despite fluctuations, it remains a historically significant club and a pioneer of football in Luxembourg.

name: Red Boys Differdange
content:
FA Red Boys Differdange was a historic football club based in Differdange, in southwestern Luxembourg. Founded in 1907, it became one of the country’s most important teams and competed in the top division for many years. The club played its home matches at Stade du Thillenberg and was known for its red and white colors. It remained active until 2003, when it merged with another local club to form FC Differdange 03.

The club enjoyed its greatest success during the interwar period, particularly in the 1920s and 1930s, when it competed with Spora Luxembourg for dominance in national football. During this time, Red Boys achieved an impressive run of success, winning numerous trophies and establishing itself as one of the strongest teams in the country. Overall, the club won six national league titles and set a record in the Luxembourg Cup with 15 victories, making it the most successful team in that competition’s history.

On the European stage, Red Boys Differdange participated in several UEFA competitions but never progressed beyond the first round. Despite limited success internationally, it gained recognition for occasional notable results, including a win in European Cup qualification and a draw against Ajax. After decades as a major force in Luxembourgish football, the club ceased to exist following its merger in 2003, leaving behind a strong historical legacy.

name: Union Luxembourg
content:
Union Luxembourg, officially known as Union Sportive Luxembourg, was a historic football club based in Luxembourg City. Founded in 1925 through the merger of US Hollerich Bonnevoie and Jeunesse Sportive Verlorenkost, the club became an important part of the country’s football scene. It played its home matches at Stade Achille Hammerel and remained active until 2005, when it merged with other clubs to form Racing FC Union Luxembourg.

In its early years, the club experienced limited success, winning its first national championship in 1927. After World War II, Union Luxembourg struggled to achieve major results for a period, but its fortunes improved significantly from the late 1950s onward. Between 1959 and 1971, the club won multiple domestic trophies, including league titles and several Luxembourg Cups, establishing itself as one of the stronger teams in the country during that era.

The club enjoyed another peak at the end of the 1980s and early 1990s, winning three consecutive league titles from 1990 to 1992. Overall, Union Luxembourg won six national championships and ten Luxembourg Cups, and regularly qualified for European competitions, although it achieved limited success internationally. Financial and structural challenges eventually led to its merger in 2005, marking the end of its independent history but contributing to the formation of a new major club in Luxembourg football.

name: FC Avenir Beggen
content:
FC Avenir Beggen is a football club based in Beggen, a district of Luxembourg City. Founded in 1915, the club originally began as FC Daring Beggen before adopting its current name a year later. Over time, it underwent several name changes, particularly during World War II, before returning to FC Avenir Beggen in 1944. The team has traditionally played its home matches at the Stade rue Henri Dunant and has been an important part of Luxembourgish football history.

The club enjoyed its greatest success during the late 20th century, especially in the 1980s and early 1990s. Avenir Beggen won six Luxembourg National Division titles and seven Luxembourg Cups, establishing itself as one of the strongest teams in the country during that era. It was particularly dominant in the early 1990s, when it secured multiple league and cup victories in a short period and regularly competed at the top level of domestic football.

On the European stage, Avenir Beggen qualified for UEFA competitions 16 times, participating in tournaments such as the European Cup (now UEFA Champions League), UEFA Cup, and Cup Winners’ Cup. Although the club rarely progressed beyond early rounds, it recorded a few notable results and gained international experience. In more recent years, the club has declined from its former heights, experiencing relegations and currently competing outside the top tier of Luxembourgish football.

name: US Hollerich Bonnevoie
content:
Union Sportive Hollerich Bonnevoie was a Luxembourgish football club based in Luxembourg City, founded in 1909. It quickly became one of the dominant teams in the early years of organized football in Luxembourg. The club competed in the national championship from its inception and was one of the founding forces of the domestic league system, representing the Hollerich and Bonnevoie districts of the capital.

During the 1910s, the club experienced its golden era. It won multiple national titles, including five championship victories between 1912 and 1917, and was especially dominant in the mid-1910s when it won several consecutive leagues. One of its most remarkable achievements was an undefeated championship season in 1916–17, highlighting its superiority in Luxembourg football at the time.

By the early 1920s, the club’s dominance began to decline, and in 1925 it merged with Jeunesse Sportive Verlorenkost to form Union Luxembourg. This merger was part of a broader effort to strengthen football in the capital. Although US Hollerich Bonnevoie ceased to exist as an independent club, its legacy remained significant as one of the most successful and influential teams in the early history of Luxembourg football.

name: FC Progrès Niederkorn
content:
FC Progrès Niederkorn is a football club based in Niederkorn, in south-western Luxembourg. Founded in 1919, the club has become a long-standing participant in Luxembourg’s top football structure, currently competing in the National Division, the country’s highest league. It plays its home matches at Stade Jos Haupert and is traditionally recognized as one of the stronger provincial clubs outside the capital.

Historically, Progrès Niederkorn has had several successful periods, especially in the 1950s and again in the late 1970s and early 1980s. The club has won the Luxembourg championship three times and has also secured multiple Luxembourg Cup titles, often achieving strong domestic results during its peak eras. These successes established it as a competitive force in Luxembourg football, particularly before the rise of more dominant modern clubs.

In more recent years, the club has gained attention again for its performances in European competitions. Although it had long struggled to progress in UEFA tournaments, it achieved a breakthrough in the 2017–18 Europa League by eliminating Rangers, marking one of the most famous results in Luxembourgish club football history. Since then, Progrès Niederkorn has continued to compete regularly in Europe while maintaining a solid presence in the domestic league.

name: FC Aris Bonnevoie
content:
FC Aris Bonnevoie was a football club based in Bonnevoie, a district of Luxembourg City. Founded in 1922, it became one of the established teams in Luxembourg football and competed for many years in the country’s top division. The club played its home matches in Luxembourg City and built a reputation as a competitive side in domestic football, especially during the mid-20th century.

The club experienced its strongest period between the 1960s and 1970s. During this era, Aris Bonnevoie won multiple national league titles and a Luxembourg Cup, establishing itself as one of the leading teams in the country. It was also a regular participant in European competitions, where it represented Luxembourg in various UEFA tournaments, gaining experience against stronger international opponents despite limited success overall.

In European competition, Aris is remembered for several notable appearances, including reaching the second round of the Cup Winners’ Cup in 1979–80 and scoring against major clubs such as FC Barcelona. Although the team rarely advanced far in Europe, these matches remain important highlights in its history. The club ceased to exist in 2001 after merging with other local teams, eventually contributing to the formation of Racing FC Union Luxembourg.

name: FC Differdange 03
content:
FC Differdange 03 is a football club based in Differdange, in southwestern Luxembourg. It was founded in 2003 following the merger of two local clubs, FA Red Boys Differdange and AS Differdange, combining the history and traditions of both sides. The club quickly became part of the Luxembourg football structure, competing in the National Division, the country’s top tier, and playing its home matches at Stade Parc des Sports.

Since its formation, the club has grown into one of the stronger teams in Luxembourg football. After initial promotion struggles, it established itself in the top division and began regularly competing for domestic trophies. FC Differdange 03 has won multiple Luxembourg Cups and has also secured league titles in recent seasons, marking a modern period of success that built on the legacy of its predecessor clubs.

In European competitions, Differdange has become one of Luxembourg’s more experienced representatives. The club has participated frequently in UEFA qualifying rounds, including the Champions League, Europa League, and Conference League. It has achieved several notable results, such as wins against stronger European opponents and deep runs into qualifying stages, although it has not yet reached a major group stage in continental tournaments.

name: SC Luxembourg
content:
Sporting Club Luxembourg was a football club based in Luxembourg City. It was founded in 1908 and became one of the early contributors to the development of organized football in the country. The club competed in the top tiers of Luxembourg football during the early 20th century and was part of the strong group of capital-based teams that shaped the beginnings of the national competition.

The club achieved its greatest historical significance in 1923 when it merged with Racing Club Luxembourg to form CA Spora Luxembourg. This merger brought together two of the strongest early clubs in the capital and helped create a more competitive and stable football structure. Sporting Club Luxembourg itself had already played a key role in early domestic success and in establishing football traditions in the city.

Although Sporting Club Luxembourg ceased to exist as an independent entity after the merger, its legacy continued through Spora Luxembourg and later Racing FC Union Luxembourg. The club is remembered as one of the foundational teams of Luxembourg football, contributing players, identity, and history to the later dominant clubs in the capital.

name: CS Grevenmacher
content:
CS Grevenmacher is a football club based in Grevenmacher, in eastern Luxembourg near the border with Germany. Founded in 1909, it is one of the older clubs in the country and has spent most of its history moving between the top two levels of Luxembourg football. The team plays its home matches at Stade Op Flohr and traditionally wears blue and white colors.

The club’s most successful period came in the late 1990s and early 2000s. During this time, CS Grevenmacher became a strong contender in domestic competitions, regularly finishing near the top of the National Division. The highlight of its history was winning the national championship in the 2002–03 season, which was also part of a domestic double alongside the Luxembourg Cup. This era established the club as one of the leading sides in Luxembourg football.

CS Grevenmacher has also taken part in European competitions on several occasions, representing Luxembourg in UEFA qualifying rounds. While the club has not achieved major progress in Europe, it has played against stronger international opponents and gained valuable experience. In later years, the team faced relegations and currently competes in the lower divisions, but it remains an important historic club in Luxembourg football.

name: FC Schifflange 95
content:
FC Schifflange 95 is a football club based in Schifflange, in southern Luxembourg. It was founded in 1995 as a result of the merger between two local clubs, Amis des Sports and National Schifflange. The club plays its home matches at Stade Rue Denis Netgen and competes mainly in the Luxembourg second tier, the Division of Honour.

The club has a mixed history of movement between divisions, often moving between the top tier and lower leagues. Its predecessor, National Schifflange, had historical success, including winning the Luxembourg championship in 1951–52 and the Luxembourg Cup in 1960, which forms part of the club’s inherited legacy.

Since its foundation, FC Schifflange 95 has focused on stabilizing itself in Luxembourg football, achieving several promotions and relegations over the years. In recent seasons, it has continued competing in the second tier, aiming to return to the National Division while developing its squad and maintaining its presence in national competitions.

name: FC Swift Hesperange
content:
FC Swift Hesperange is a football club based in Hesperange, a commune in southern Luxembourg near Luxembourg City. Founded in 1916, the club has spent much of its history moving between divisions but has become a consistent presence in Luxembourg’s top football tier in recent decades. It plays its home matches at Stade Alphonse Theis and is known for its red identity and steady rise in modern Luxembourg football.

The club’s early history included long periods in the lower divisions, but it gradually developed into a stronger side. One of its first major achievements was winning the Luxembourg Cup in the 1989–90 season, which also marked its debut in European competitions the following year. During the 2010s and early 2020s, Swift Hesperange improved significantly, eventually returning to the top division and becoming a competitive team in the league standings.

In recent years, the club has experienced its most successful period. It won its first-ever national league title in the 2022–23 season and has also competed in UEFA tournaments such as the Champions League and Europa Conference League. While it has not yet made a deep run in Europe, it has achieved notable wins in qualifying rounds and established itself as one of the stronger modern clubs in Luxembourg football.

name: RC Luxembourg
content:
Racing Club Luxembourg was a football club based in Luxembourg City, founded in 1907. It is historically significant as one of the pioneers of organised football in the country and played a central role in the early development of the national game. The club competed in the first official Luxembourg championship and quickly became one of the strongest teams in the capital during the pre-war era. It was also one of the key contributors to the formation of early football structures in Luxembourg.

The club achieved major early success, becoming the first-ever champion of Luxembourg in the 1909–10 season. It also won the first edition of the Luxembourg Cup in 1922, further confirming its status as a leading team of its time. Racing Club was part of a dominant group of capital clubs that shaped Luxembourg football in its formative years, often supplying players to the national team and influencing the sport’s early growth in the country.

In 1923, Racing Club Luxembourg merged with Sporting Club Luxembourg to form CA Spora Luxembourg, marking the end of its independent existence. Despite dissolving as a separate entity, its legacy continued through successor clubs that went on to achieve further domestic and international success. Racing Club Luxembourg is remembered as one of the foundational teams in Luxembourg football history, with a lasting impact on the sport’s development in the country.

name: US Dudelange
content:
Union Sportive Dudelange was a football club based in Dudelange, in southern Luxembourg. It was founded in 1912 through the merger of two local teams and became one of the important clubs in Luxembourg football during the first half of the 20th century. The club played a significant role in the development of the sport in the region and competed regularly in the country’s national competitions. It was also one of the traditional clubs from the industrial town of Dudelange, which had several strong teams at the time.

The club experienced its strongest period between the late 1930s and 1950s. During this era, US Dudelange won the Luxembourg Cup in 1939 and finished as runners-up in the national league on multiple occasions. It remained competitive in domestic football for several decades, often challenging for trophies but not achieving the same level of dominance as some of its local rivals.

In 1991, US Dudelange ceased to exist as an independent club when it merged with Stade Dudelange and Alliance Dudelange to form F91 Dudelange. This merger combined the traditions and histories of three long-established clubs into a single modern team, which later became one of the most successful clubs in Luxembourg football. Despite its dissolution, US Dudelange remains an important part of the historical foundation of football in Dudelange.

name: US Rumelange
content:
US Rumelange is a football club based in Rumelange, in south-western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1907 and is considered one of the older clubs in the country, with a long history in Luxembourg football. The team plays its home matches at Stade Municipal de Rumelange and has traditionally been a stable presence in the national football system, often moving between the top division and the second tier.

The club experienced its strongest period in the 1960s and 1970s, when it regularly competed at the top of Luxembourg football. During this time, US Rumelange finished as runners-up in the national championship several times and also achieved success in domestic cup competitions, winning the Luxembourg Cup twice. This era established the club as a competitive side capable of challenging stronger teams in the country.

On the international stage, US Rumelange has participated in UEFA competitions on multiple occasions, including the UEFA Cup and Cup Winners’ Cup. However, its European campaigns were largely unsuccessful, with early eliminations and heavy defeats against stronger opposition, including a record aggregate loss to Feyenoord in the early 1970s. In more recent years, the club has mostly competed in the second tier of Luxembourg football, maintaining its role as a traditional but modest local team.

name: FC Etzella Ettelbruck
content:
FC Etzella Ettelbruck is a football club based in Ettelbruck, in northern Luxembourg. Founded in 1917, it is one of the traditional clubs in the country and has spent most of its history competing between the top two tiers of Luxembourg football. The team plays its home matches at Stade Am Deich and is known for its blue-and-white identity.

The club has experienced several notable periods in its history, especially in the early 2000s. Its most successful achievement came in the 2000–01 season when it won the Luxembourg Cup, which also allowed it to participate in European competitions for the first time. During the mid-2000s, Etzella also had strong league performances, finishing near the top of the National Division and regularly qualifying for UEFA tournaments, although without deep progress.

In European competition, FC Etzella Ettelbruck has made multiple appearances in UEFA qualifying rounds but has struggled against stronger international opponents, often exiting in early stages. In domestic football, the club has moved between divisions in recent years but remains a stable and established part of Luxembourg’s football system, continuing to compete mainly in the second tier while aiming to return to the top division.

name: Alliance Dudelange
content:
Alliance Dudelange was a football club based in Dudelange in southern Luxembourg. It was founded in 1916 through the merger of two local teams, Étoile Rouge Dudelange and Étoile Bleue Dudelange, and became one of the traditional clubs from a town with a strong football culture. The club competed in Luxembourg’s football league system for most of its history and played its home matches at Stade Amadéo Barozzi.

The club experienced its strongest period in the 1960s. During this time, Alliance Dudelange achieved notable domestic success, winning the Luxembourg Cup twice in 1961 and 1962 and finishing as runners-up in the national championship in 1962. It also reached another cup final in 1969. In addition, the club participated in European competitions, including the Cup Winners’ Cup, although it was eliminated in the early rounds.

In 1991, Alliance Dudelange merged with Stade Dudelange and US Dudelange to form F91 Dudelange. This merger combined the resources and histories of three long-established clubs in the city, creating a stronger modern team. Although Alliance Dudelange ceased to exist as an independent club, it remains an important part of the foundation of one of Luxembourg’s most successful contemporary football projects.

name: Racing FC Union Luxembourg
content:
Racing FC Union Luxembourg is a football club based in Luxembourg City. It was founded in 2005 as a result of a three-way merger between CA Spora Luxembourg, Union Luxembourg, and CS Alliance 01. Each of these clubs had long and rich histories of their own, so Racing FC effectively represents a consolidation of some of the most traditional football institutions in the capital. The club plays its home matches at Stade Achille Hammerel and competes in the Luxembourg National Division.

The formation of the club was part of a broader restructuring of Luxembourg football, where financial and sporting pressures led several historic teams to merge. Since its creation, Racing FC has worked to stabilize itself in the top division, with mixed results in domestic competitions. The club has also developed a reputation for resilience, often competing in the upper mid-table and occasionally challenging for European qualification spots, though without yet establishing itself as a dominant force.

In recent years, Racing FC Union Luxembourg has continued to evolve both on and off the pitch, focusing on squad development and organizational stability. It has also achieved success in cup competitions, most notably winning the Luxembourg Cup in 2018, which marked one of its most significant achievements since formation. While still building its identity compared to the historic clubs it absorbed, Racing FC is now an established part of modern Luxembourg football.

name: FC UNA Strassen
content:
FC UNA Strassen is a football club based in Strassen, a commune in south-western Luxembourg near the capital city. The club was founded in 1922 under the name Union Athlétique Strassen and has since developed into one of the established teams in Luxembourg football. It currently competes in the BGL Ligue, the top division of the country, and plays its home matches at the Stade An de Millewisen.

For most of its history, UNA Strassen played in the lower divisions of Luxembourg football and spent many years climbing the league system. The club began to progress more significantly in the 2000s and eventually reached the top flight in 2015 after winning promotion from the second tier. Since then, it has consolidated its position in the National Division, becoming a stable mid-to-upper table side and increasingly competitive against more traditional clubs.

In recent years, FC UNA Strassen has experienced its most successful period, including strong league finishes and qualification for European competitions. The club reached the UEFA Conference League qualifiers for the first time and has since continued to develop its squad and infrastructure. Although still relatively modest compared to Luxembourg’s historically dominant teams, it has grown into a modern and competitive club within the national football landscape.

name: CS Pétange
content:
CS Pétange is a former football club based in Pétange, in south-western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1910 and spent much of its history competing in the country’s football league system, including several spells in the top division. The club played its home matches at Stade Municipal de Pétange and was known for its long-standing presence in Luxembourg football as a traditional community team.

Throughout its history, CS Pétange experienced fluctuating success, moving between divisions but also achieving notable domestic moments. Its most significant achievement came in the 2004–05 season when it won the Luxembourg Cup, the club’s first major trophy. This victory also marked one of its best eras, as it allowed the team to qualify for European competition for the first time, where it competed in the UEFA Cup qualifiers.

The club reached the Luxembourg Cup final earlier in 1991–92 but finished as runner-up, showing its potential to compete at a high level before eventually breaking through with its cup win. In 2015, CS Pétange ceased to exist as an independent club after merging with FC Titus Lamadelaine to form Union Titus Pétange. This merger ended over a century of history, but its legacy continues through the modern club that replaced it.

name: Jeunesse Hautcharage
content:
Jeunesse Hautcharage was a football club based in Hautcharage, Luxembourg, founded in 1919. For most of its existence, the club competed in the lower tiers of Luxembourg football, gradually building its reputation as a modest regional side. Despite not being a regular top-flight team, it became part of the country’s football history through a few remarkable achievements.

The greatest success in the club’s history came in 1971, when Jeunesse Hautcharage won the Luxembourg Cup while playing as a third-division team. In the final, they achieved a surprising 4–1 victory after extra time against Jeunesse Esch, one of the strongest clubs in the country. This victory remains the club’s defining moment and earned them qualification for European competition.

In the 1971–72 season, Jeunesse Hautcharage participated in the European Cup Winners’ Cup, where they faced Chelsea in the first round. The matches proved extremely difficult, resulting in heavy defeats both home and away. The club also had only one brief spell in Luxembourg’s top division during the 1981–82 season, where they finished in 11th place. Later, the club eventually merged into UN Käerjéng 97, ending its independent existence.

name: UN Käerjéng 97
content:
UN Käerjéng 97 is a football club based in Bascharage (Käerjeng) in south-western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1997 as a merger of Union Sportive Bascharage and Jeunesse Hautcharage, combining the traditions of two local clubs into a single modern team. The club plays its home matches at Stade um Dribbel and has grown into a stable participant in Luxembourg’s football system.

Since its formation, the club has mainly competed between the top two tiers of Luxembourg football, gradually establishing itself as a regular presence in the National Division. It has experienced promotions and relegations over the years, reflecting its development stage as a relatively young club compared to many historic Luxembourg teams. One of its notable achievements includes reaching the top division and competing there in multiple seasons during the 2000s and 2020s.

UN Käerjéng 97 also has a modest but interesting European history through its predecessor Jeunesse Hautcharage, which famously played in the Cup Winners’ Cup in the early 1970s. As a merged club, Käerjéng itself has also appeared in UEFA competition qualifiers, gaining experience against stronger international opponents. Today, it continues to develop its squad and infrastructure while aiming to remain competitive in Luxembourg’s top flight.

name: SC Tétange
content:
SC Tétange was a football club from Tétange, Luxembourg, founded in 1914. During World War II, between 1940 and 1944, the club was forcibly renamed FK Tetingen. For much of its history, it competed in Luxembourg’s league system, experiencing both periods in the top division and long spells in the lower tiers.

The club’s strongest era came in the post-war years. Between 1947 and 1961, with the exception of the 1955–56 season, SC Tétange played consistently in the top division. It returned to the National Division again in 1969 but was relegated in 1973, after which it gradually declined through the league system over the following decades.

The greatest achievement in SC Tétange’s history was winning the Luxembourg Cup in 1951. In the final against CS Grevenmacher, the first match ended 1–1 after extra time, but SC Tétange won the replay 2–0 to secure the trophy. In later years, the club continued to fall through the divisions and eventually competed in the lower leagues before later merging into a new football structure.

name: FC Mondercange
content:
FC Mondercange is a football club based in Mondercange in south-western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1933 and has spent most of its history moving between the lower and middle levels of the Luxembourg football league system. The club plays its home matches at Stade Communal Mondercange and is known for being a stable regional team rather than one of the traditional national powerhouses.

Over the decades, FC Mondercange has experienced gradual development with several promotions to the top division, the National Division, and subsequent relegations. One of its key periods came in the late 1990s and early 2000s, when the club reached the top tier and even competed in the Luxembourg Cup final twice. These performances marked the peak of its sporting success and gave the club brief exposure to European competition.

In European football, FC Mondercange made a single appearance in UEFA competition during the 1999–2000 UEFA Cup qualifiers, where it faced strong opposition and was eliminated early. In recent years, the club has mostly competed in the second tier of Luxembourg football, continuing to focus on maintaining stability and rebuilding its position in the national league system.

name: Racing Rodange
content:
FC Racing Rodange was a football club based in Rodange in south-western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1931 and spent most of its history competing in the Luxembourg football league system, mainly moving between the top two divisions. The club represented a typical local team from the industrial south of the country and played its home matches in Rodange.

During its existence, Racing Rodange had several spells in Luxembourg’s top division, especially in the late 1940s and early 1950s. One of its notable achievements was reaching the final of the Luxembourg Cup in 1949, where it finished as runner-up. Overall, the club was competitive domestically but did not manage to establish itself as a long-term top-tier side.

In 1991, FC Racing Rodange merged with FC Chiers Rodange to form FC Rodange 91. This merger combined two historic local clubs into a single modern structure aimed at strengthening football in the region. While Racing Rodange ceased to exist as an independent club, its history remains part of the foundation of the current Rodange football identity.

name: FC CeBra 01
content:
FC CeBra 01 is a football club based in Cessange, a district of Luxembourg City. It was founded in 2001 following a merger between Progrès Cessange and Bracarenses Grund, making it a relatively modern club in Luxembourg football. The team plays its home matches at the Complexe Sportif Boy Konen and has mainly competed in the lower and middle tiers of the national league system.

Since its creation, FC CeBra 01 has been active across various levels of Luxembourg football, often moving between divisions. The club has also developed both men’s and women’s teams, with the women’s side achieving notable success in national competitions, including appearances in Luxembourg Cup finals. Over time, CeBra has built a reputation as a community-focused club in the capital rather than a top-tier powerhouse.

In 2023, FC CeBra 01 was merged into FC Luxembourg City as part of a wider restructuring of football in Luxembourg. This merger marked the end of its independent existence after more than two decades. Despite its relatively short history, the club contributed to local football development and remains part of the evolving football landscape in Luxembourg.

name: AS Differdange
content:
AS Differdange was a football club based in Differdange in south-western Luxembourg. It was formed as part of the local football structure in the city and competed within the Luxembourg league system, mainly operating in the lower and middle divisions. The club was one of several teams representing Differdange before later structural changes in the local football scene.

AS Differdange is best known for being one of the two clubs that merged in 2003 to create FC Differdange 03, alongside the historic FA Red Boys Differdange. At the time of the merger, AS was playing in the lower tiers of Luxembourg football, while Red Boys was the more successful and established side. The combination of both clubs aimed to unify football in the city and strengthen competitiveness at national level.

After the merger, AS Differdange ceased to exist as an independent entity, and its history became part of FC Differdange 03. Although it did not achieve major national honours on its own, the club remains an important part of the background history of modern football in Differdange, contributing to the formation of one of Luxembourg’s current top-flight teams.

name: Olympique Eischen
content:
FC Olympique Eischen was a football club based in Eischen in western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1917 and spent most of its history competing in the lower and middle levels of Luxembourg football. The club represented a small regional team and played its home matches at the local municipal stadium, gradually building its identity within the national football system.

The club experienced its most notable period between the 1980s, when it reached Luxembourg’s top division, the National Division. Olympique Eischen played several seasons at the highest level, including the early 1980s and late 1980s, and also reached the Luxembourg Cup final in 1981, which was its greatest achievement despite losing the match heavily. These years marked the peak of its competitive performance in domestic football.

After its spells in the top division, the club gradually declined through the league tiers and eventually fell to the lower amateur levels. In 2007, FC Olympique Eischen merged with CS Hobscheid to form Alliance Aischdall, ending its existence as an independent club. Despite this, it remains remembered as a historic small club that briefly reached Luxembourg’s elite level.

name: Red Star Merl-Belair
content:
FC Red Star Merl-Belair is a football club based in Merl, a district of Luxembourg City. It was founded in 1927 and is one of the long-established clubs in the capital’s football scene. The team plays its home matches at Stade Prince Jean and has traditionally competed within the Luxembourg league system, mainly between the lower and middle divisions.

Historically, the club experienced its strongest period in the 1950s and early 1970s. During that time, Red Star Merl-Belair spent several seasons in the Luxembourg National Division, the top tier of the country’s football, and achieved some notable cup runs, including reaching the Luxembourg Cup final in the early 1950s. It also had brief returns to the top division in the 1970s, though it was generally unable to maintain long-term stability at that level.

In later decades, the club gradually declined through the league system and spent more time in the lower divisions of Luxembourg football. Despite this, it has remained active as a community club in Merl, continuing to compete in domestic competitions. Today, FC Red Star Merl-Belair is considered a traditional lower-league side with a long historical background rather than a top-tier contender.

name: FC Wiltz 71
content:
FC Wiltz 71 is a football club based in Wiltz in north-western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1971 through the merger of several local teams and has since become a well-known “yo-yo” club, often moving between the top division (National Division) and the second tier of Luxembourg football. The team plays its home matches at Stade Am Pëtz in Weidingen and represents one of the main clubs from the northern part of the country.

Throughout its history, FC Wiltz 71 has experienced frequent promotions and relegations, reflecting an unstable but competitive sporting level. The club reached the National Division within its first decade of existence and has had several notable spells in the top flight. One of its strongest periods came in the early 2000s and mid-2000s, when it achieved solid mid-table finishes, including a 5th-place result, which remains one of its best league performances.

The club’s most significant achievement came in the 2000–01 season, when it reached the final of the Luxembourg Cup, ultimately finishing as runner-up after a close defeat. FC Wiltz 71 has also participated in multiple top-division campaigns but has struggled to maintain long-term stability at that level. In recent years, it has continued to alternate between divisions while focusing on rebuilding and maintaining its position in Luxembourg football.

name: FC Victoria Rosport
content:
FC Victoria Rosport is a football club based in Rosport in eastern Luxembourg, founded on 1 October 1928. It is a long-established club in Luxembourg football and competes in the country’s league system, mainly alternating between the top division (National Division) and the second tier over its history. The team plays its home matches at the Party-Rent-Arena.

For much of its early history, the club remained a modest side, but it gradually developed into a more competitive team after World War II. Victoria Rosport has spent multiple spells in the higher divisions and built a reputation as a stable mid-table club in Luxembourg football. Its growth accelerated in the early 2000s when it reached the National Division and began achieving stronger league performances.

One of the club’s most successful periods came in the mid-2000s, when it finished in its best-ever league position and qualified for European competition for the first time. It also reached the final of the Luxembourg Cup in 2008, finishing as runner-up. The club has since remained a regular participant in top-division football, continuing to compete at a solid national level while maintaining its status as a respected provincial team.

name: US Mondorf-les-Bains
content:
US Mondorf-les-Bains is a football club based in Mondorf-les-Bains in south-eastern Luxembourg. It was founded in 1915 and is one of the established clubs in the country’s football system. The team plays its home matches at Stade John Grün and has grown into a stable participant in Luxembourg’s top division in recent years.

For much of its history, the club moved between divisions, spending long periods in lower leagues before gradually building its level. It reached the national top flight several times in the 1960s and then again more consistently after its modern resurgence in the 2010s. A key milestone was its return to the highest division in 2014 after more than four decades away, marking a major revival in the club’s fortunes.

In modern times, US Mondorf has become a regular mid-table team in the Luxembourg National Division and has also reached notable cup success, including a run to the Luxembourg Cup final in 2016, where it finished as runner-up. The club continues to compete at a solid national level, maintaining stability in the top tier and occasionally challenging stronger sides in domestic competitions.

name: US Hostert
content:
US Hostert is a football club based in Hostert, a village in the commune of Niederanven in central Luxembourg. It was founded in 1946 and is considered a small community club that gradually built its position within the Luxembourg football system. The team plays its home matches at Stade Jos Becker and has traditionally represented one of the smaller local sides in the country.

For most of its history, the club competed in the lower divisions of Luxembourg football, spending many years outside the top tier. Its rise was relatively slow, but it eventually achieved a major milestone in 2011 when it was promoted to the National Division for the first time in its history. This marked a turning point, as the club transitioned from an amateur-level side into a regular participant in the country’s top league.

Since reaching the top division, US Hostert has mainly functioned as a mid-to-lower table team, often fighting to maintain its place in the National Division. It has also invested in youth development and community football, helping strengthen its long-term stability. Although it has not won major national titles, its promotion to the top tier and continued presence there are considered the most important achievements in its history.

name: FC Marisca Mersch
content:
FC Marisca Mersch is a football club based in Mersch, Luxembourg, founded in 1908. It is considered one of the traditional clubs in the country, with a long history of competing across the various levels of Luxembourg football. The team plays its home matches at Stade Schintgespesch and is known for its yellow and blue colours, representing the town for more than a century.

For most of its existence, Marisca Mersch competed in the lower divisions and remained a modest amateur side. During the 20th century, it gradually moved between the third and second tiers, without establishing long-term stability in the top flight. In 2023, however, the club achieved a historic milestone by earning promotion to the Luxembourg National Division for the first time in its history after finishing second in the second tier.

The same breakthrough season also saw the club reach the Luxembourg Cup final for the first time, where it lost to Differdange 03. After its debut season in the top division, Marisca Mersch was relegated again, but it remains an ambitious club focused on rebuilding and maintaining its position among Luxembourg’s competitive teams.

name: National Schifflange
content:
The National Schifflange was a football club based in Schifflange in south-western Luxembourg. It was founded in 1912 and became one of the historic clubs in the country’s early football development. The team competed for many decades in the Luxembourg league system, including multiple spells in the National Division, the country’s top tier. It was one of several clubs from Schifflange that helped establish the town as an active football centre.

The club’s most successful period came in the post-war era. National Schifflange won the Luxembourg championship in the 1951–52 season, marking the highest achievement in its history. It also won the Luxembourg Cup in 1960, adding another major trophy to its honours list. During this time, the club regularly competed at the top level and also produced notable results against strong domestic opposition.

Over time, the club experienced decline and eventually moved down through the divisions. In the later decades it no longer maintained top-flight status and eventually dropped into the lower tiers of Luxembourg football. In 1995, National Schifflange merged with Amis des Sports Schifflange to form FC Schifflange 95, ending its independent existence but leaving a legacy as one of the traditional clubs of the town.

name: CS Hobscheid
content:
CS Hobscheid, officially Cercle Sportif Hobscheid, was a football club based in Hobscheid in western Luxembourg. Founded in 1932, the club spent most of its history competing in the Luxembourg league system, gradually working its way through the divisions. It played its home matches at Stade Koericherberg and was known for its black-and-yellow colors.

The club reached the top tier of Luxembourg football relatively late, making its debut in the National Division in the 1996–97 season. Its best performance came in the 2000–01 campaign, when it achieved its highest-ever league finish. Despite this progress, CS Hobscheid was unable to establish itself permanently at the top level and soon dropped back into lower divisions.

CS Hobscheid also participated in European competitions, appearing three times in the UEFA Intertoto Cup, although it did not progress beyond the first round. In 2007, the club merged with FC Olympique Eischen to form FC Alliance Äischdall, bringing an end to its independent existence. Despite its modest success, it remains part of the historical development of football in its region.
